about.text:
Ki-Lo setup wizard (KEY-603, part of KEY-6). Draft for Zee's review. Mobile only: every board shows dark and light at 390 x 844, and the label over each phone names its state.

Zee's ten answers of 23 Oct on KEY-594 decide the steps: sex (female, male, prefer not to say, stored as other), date of birth, height and weight on one step, one activity question with five levels, goal, rate (skipped for Maintain), protein (moderate 1.6, high 2.0, very high 2.2 g/kg), diet style (balanced, low fat, low carb), then the estimate. Under 18: no Lose. Under 13: not accepted. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: a note on the goal step, no question, nothing stored. Guardrails shown when they change the result. First run ends on the Diary; a recalculation returns to Targets.

Not drawn, on purpose: body fat, keto, training type, workouts per week, a check-in weekday, height from Health, and web boards (after the mobile wizard has shipped and Zee has used it).

Authority, highest first: Zee's rulings on Linear, the Ki-Lo Design System, the approved M2 to M5 boards and the built mobile kit, MacroFactor where Ki-Lo is silent (its setup screens are not verified in design-reference/macrofactor.md, so no layout here is borrowed from it), then ticket prose.

Flow: step 1 About you, sex; 2 birth date; 3 height and weight; 4 activity; 5 goal; 6 rate; 7 protein; 8 diet; then the estimate. Maintain skips the rate, so its count reads "of 7" from the moment Maintain is chosen.

Health data rule: every person here is made-up sample data. The main sample: male, born 14 Mar 1991 (35 on 23 Oct 2026), 180 cm, 80.0 kg, lightly active, lose 0.5% a week, moderate protein, balanced. Every number on the rate, protein and estimate boards is the engine's output for the stated answers (M6 build plan, Expenditure and Targets); the arithmetic is in the estimate notes.

questions.text:
Open questions for Zee, each with the recommended answer (drawn as recommended).

1. Date of birth input. Drawn: three typed fields, Day, Month, Year. The kit's DatePicker is a month calendar that opens on today and disables future days: reaching 1991 is about 430 presses of previous month, and a future date can never be entered, so its error could not exist. Recommended: typed fields. Alternative: extend DatePicker with a year jump.

2. Under 18 and Lose. Drawn: Lose shown disabled with its reason, so the person sees why. Alternative: leave it out. Recommended: disabled with the reason.

3. The rate default's mark. Drawn: Badge "Suggested" on 0.5% (lose) and 0.25% (gain), chosen on arrival. Alternative: "Default", the word the portion picker uses. Recommended: "Suggested".

4. Stones. Ki-Lo already formats st, and many UK people weigh in stones. Drawn: kg and cm, or lb and ft, in, as ruled. Recommended: no stones now.

5. Close in recalculate leaves without a confirm (nothing is saved before Start, and every answer is prefilled next time). Recommended: no confirm.

6. First run lands on the Diary with no toast: the ring already shows the new target. Recommended: no toast.

aboutyoutitle.text: About you · steps 1 to 3 · the wizard shell, sex, date of birth, height and weight

aboutyounotes.text:
About you notes (S3, S7).

The shell, on every step: SheetHeader (sheet) with the group as its title ("About you", "Activity", "Goal", "Macros") and "Step n of 8" as its subtitle; the kit's ProgressBar under it, filled to n / 9 (the estimate fills it), named "Step n of 8"; the question in h1 with one helper line in secondary body; the step's controls; a footer on surface-sheet with Button primary lg "Continue", dimmed to 40% and aria-disabled until the step is valid. The step body scrolls under a fixed header and footer. Back on every step except step 1. First run has no Close: its one way out is step 1's escape. Recalculate adds Close on the right of every step (setup: entry · recalculate). Answers are kept when going Back. Single questions cannot be skipped.

setup: about you · sex. "What is your sex?" / "Ki-Lo uses it with your age, height and weight to estimate the energy you use each day." OptionCards: Female; Male; Prefer not to say, "Ki-Lo uses the average of the female and male estimates." (stored as other, BMR offset -78). Nothing is chosen on first run, so Continue starts dimmed. First run only: no Back, and Button ghost quiet "I'll set my own targets" under Continue. It marks the account set up and opens Targets (S7).

setup: about you · birth-date. "When were you born?" / "Your age is part of the estimate." Three NumericInputs, number pad, British order: Day, Month, Year (placeholders DD, MM, YYYY). A valid date adds "You are 35." under them. Errors, in danger caption under the fields once the year has four digits or the person moves on, with the three fields bordered in danger: "You need to be 13 or over to use Ki-Lo." (under 13: Continue stays off, there is no way past); "Enter a date before today." (today or later). Not drawn, same red line: "Enter a real date." (such as 31 02) and "Enter a year after 1900.". Aged 13 to 17 changes the goal step.

setup: about you · body. "How tall are you, and what do you weigh?" / "Your weight this morning, before you eat, is best." SegmentedControl sm named "Units": "kg, cm" or "lb, ft, in". It defaults from the region (imperial for the US, Liberia and Myanmar, metric elsewhere) or the saved weight unit. Height: one field in cm, or two in ft and in. Weight: one field, one decimal, kg or lb. Switching units converts what is typed (180 cm reads 5 ft 11 in; 80.0 kg reads 176.4 lb). Prefilled: the latest weigh-in's weight, with the Scale icon and "From your weigh-in on 21 Oct" ("From your weigh-in today" for today's); changing the number removes the line. Errors under each field: "Enter a height between 100 and 250 cm." (imperial "Enter a height between 3 ft 4 in and 8 ft 2 in."); "Enter a weight between 20 and 400 kg." (the weigh-in sheet's own sentence; imperial "Enter a weight between 45 and 881 lb.").

Accessible names: the radiogroup is named by the question; radios read title then description ("Prefer not to say, Ki-Lo uses the average of the female and male estimates"); fields "Day of birth", "Month of birth", "Year of birth", "Height in centimetres", "Height, feet", "Height, inches", "Weight in kilograms", "Weight in pounds"; the escape "I'll set my own targets".

goaltitle.text: Activity, goal and rate · steps 4 to 6

goalnotes.text:
Activity, goal and rate notes (S4).

setup: activity. "How active are you?" / "Think of a normal week: your job, getting about and exercise." Five OptionCards, none chosen on first run: Sedentary (x 1.2) "Mostly sitting, with little or no exercise."; Lightly active (x 1.375) "Some walking, or exercise 1 to 3 days a week."; Moderately active (x 1.55) "On your feet a lot, or exercise 3 to 5 days a week."; Very active (x 1.725) "A physical job, or hard exercise 6 or 7 days a week."; Extra active (x 1.9) "A physical job and daily training, or training twice a day." The factors are not shown.

setup: goal · default. "What is your goal?" / "Your calorie target follows from this." Lose weight, "Eat a little less than you use."; Maintain weight, "Eat about what you use."; Gain weight, "Eat a little more than you use." None chosen on first run. Under them, always: Banner info "Pregnant or breastfeeding?" / "Talk to a doctor, midwife or dietitian before you set a goal. Ki-Lo's estimates do not allow for pregnancy or breastfeeding." No question is asked and nothing is stored.

setup: goal · under-18 (13 to 17 from the birth date; drawn at 16). Lose weight is disabled with its reason "Not offered under 18." (radio and title at 40%, the reason at full strength with an Info icon), aria-disabled, named "Lose weight, not offered under 18". The banner becomes "Talk to a health professional" / "If you are under 18 and want to lose weight, or you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to a doctor, midwife or dietitian first." Drawn with Maintain chosen, so the count reads "Step 5 of 7". If the birth date is changed so that Lose was chosen and is no longer allowed, the goal is cleared.

setup: rate · lose. "How fast do you want to lose weight?" / "As a share of your body weight each week. Slower is easier to keep up." 0.25% a week, "Gentle, and easy to keep up.", 0.2 kg; 0.5% a week with Badge "Suggested" and chosen on arrival, "A steady pace.", 0.4 kg; 0.75% a week, "Faster, and harder to keep up.", 0.6 kg; 1.0% a week, "The fastest Ki-Lo sets.", 0.8 kg.

setup: rate · gain. "How fast do you want to gain weight?" / "As a share of your body weight each week. Slower gains add less fat." 0.1% a week, "Slow, and adds the least fat.", 0.1 kg; 0.25% a week, Suggested, chosen on arrival, "A steady pace.", 0.2 kg; 0.5% a week, "The fastest Ki-Lo sets.", 0.4 kg.

The value beside each rate is pct / 100 x the weight from step 3, one decimal, in the person's unit, with "a week" under it (80.0 kg: 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 kg; 0.08 shows as 0.1 kg. At 176.4 lb: lose 0.4, 0.9, 1.3, 1.8 lb, gain 0.2, 0.4, 0.9 lb). A card's name reads "0.5% a week, suggested, a steady pace, about 0.4 kilograms a week". Changing the goal resets the rate to its default. Maintain skips this step, and Back from protein returns to the goal.

macrostitle.text: Macros · steps 7 and 8 · protein and diet style

macrosnotes.text:
Macros notes (S5).

setup: macros · protein. "How much protein?" / "Ki-Lo sets protein first, from your weight, then shares the rest between fat and carbohydrate." Moderate, chosen on arrival, "1.6 g per kg of body weight. Enough for most people.", 128 g a day; High, "2.0 g per kg. Suits regular strength training.", 160 g a day; Very high, "2.2 g per kg. Helps keep muscle while you lose weight.", 176 g a day. Grams are g/kg x 80.0 kg, whole grams, and stay in grams for imperial users (food labels are in grams).

setup: macros · diet. "How do you like to eat?" / "This splits the calories left after protein between fat and carbohydrate." Balanced, chosen on arrival, "A mix of both, as most people eat." (fat 40% of the rest); Low fat, "More bread, rice, pasta and fruit. Less oil and butter." (28%); Low carb, "More meat, fish, eggs, dairy and oils. Less bread and rice. Not keto." (60%). The fractions are not shown. No keto option. Continue leads to the estimate.

estimatetitle.text: The estimate · labelled as an estimate, with the onboarding flourish · guardrails, saving and the save error

estimatenotes.text:
Estimate notes (S6).

setup: estimate · default. Header "Your estimate" with Back and no step line; ProgressBar full, named "Setup complete". h1 "Your starting targets". A Card: "Calorie target" with Badge accent "Estimate"; the display numeral and "kcal a day"; the rate line, "To lose about 0.4 kg a week (0.5% of your weight)." (gain: "To gain about 0.2 kg a week (0.25% of your weight)."; maintain: "To keep your weight about where it is."); three tiles in the food page hero's style, Protein, Carbohydrate and Fat in grams beside their macro colours. Then a ListRow value "Estimated expenditure" / "The energy you use in a day", 2,413 kcal. Then the accuracy line (secondary caption) and the not-medical-advice line from legal.ts, verbatim (muted caption): "Ki-Lo's estimates and targets are not medical advice. Speak to a doctor before you make big changes to your diet or your weight." Footer: Button primary lg "Start" on first run, "Save targets" in recalculate.

Two accuracy lines, both final words, drawn side by side on the board. LIVE NOW, until M6's weekly check-in ships: "This is a starting estimate from your answers, and it can be out by a few hundred kcal a day. You can change these any time in Targets." LIVE ONCE THE WEEKLY CHECK-IN SHIPS: "This is a starting estimate from your answers. Each week, Ki-Lo checks it against your weigh-ins and food log and adjusts your targets."

The flourish (the design system reserves one for onboarding): on arrival the numeral counts up (CalorieRing's useCountUp) and flashes the accent (kl-flash, chart duration, whip ease); one diagonal accent slash crosses the card (kl-slash, flourish duration); the three tiles cut in from the side 36 ms apart (kl-cut-in); haptic confirm. Reduce motion: a fade only. The boards show the settled frame; the live canvas plays it once on load.

setup: estimate · guardrail. When a guardrail changes the result, the rate line is replaced by a guardrail line in caption with an Info icon, keyed by the clamp that set the final number. Floor: "Raised to {floor} kcal, the lowest target Ki-Lo sets for you. You would lose about {kg} kg a week ({pct}% of your weight), not {rate}%." Max deficit: "Kept to a 30% deficit, the most Ki-Lo sets. You would lose about {kg} kg a week ({pct}% of your weight), not {rate}%." Max surplus (not drawn): "Kept to a 20% surplus, the most Ki-Lo sets. You would gain about {kg} kg a week ({pct}% of your weight), not {rate}%." When the deficit cap and the floor both apply, the floor's line shows, because it set the number. The effective rate is to two decimals, kg to one.

setup: estimate · saving. Start keeps its width, hides its label and shows the kit spinner, aria-busy; Back is dimmed and does nothing. setup: estimate · save-error. The kit's error Banner, sentence only, above Start: "Not saved. Check your connection and try again." (SAVE_FAILED_BANNER, as Targets has it). Start works again and is the retry; the answers stay and nothing is half saved. Offline (not drawn): as Targets, the offline Banner and Start dimmed.

After Start: first run lands on the Diary, today; recalculate returns to Targets with the new numbers and the Toast "Targets saved".

Arithmetic (engine rules: BMR = 10 kg + 6.25 cm - 5 age + s; TDEE = BMR x factor; delta = pct / 100 x weight x 7,700 / 7; deficit at most 30% of TDEE; floor max(1,200, 0.9 BMR); surplus at most 20%; round to 10 without crossing a bound; protein g/kg x weight, fat a fraction of the rest with a 0.5 g/kg floor, carbohydrate fills).

Default: BMR 800 + 1,125 - 175 + 5 = 1,755.0; TDEE x 1.375 = 2,413.1 (shown 2,413). Delta 0.005 x 80 x 1,100 = 440.0; raw 1,973.1. Floor 1,579.5 and the 30% bound 1,689.2 are not reached; rounded 1,970. Protein 1.6 x 80 = 128 g; fat 0.40 x (1,970 - 512) / 9 = 64.8, 65 g (floor 40 g); carbohydrate (1,970 - 512 - 583.2) / 4 = 218.7, 219 g. Check 512 + 585 + 876 = 1,973. Actual pace (2,413.1 - 1,970) x 7 / 7,700 = 0.40 kg a week.

Floor: female, 30, 160 cm, 55.0 kg, sedentary, lose 1.0%. BMR 550 + 1,000 - 150 - 161 = 1,239; TDEE x 1.2 = 1,486.8 (1,487). Delta 0.01 x 55 x 1,100 = 605; raw 881.8. The 30% bound is 1,040.8; the floor max(1,200, 1,115.1) = 1,200 sets it: 1,200 (clamps max_deficit and floor). Pace (1,486.8 - 1,200) x 7 / 7,700 = 0.26 kg a week, 0.47% of 55 kg. Protein 88 g; fat 0.40 x 848 / 9 = 37.7, 38 g; carbohydrate 127.2, 127 g.

Max deficit: male, 40, 175 cm, 130.0 kg, moderately active, lose 1.0%. BMR 1,300 + 1,093.75 - 200 + 5 = 2,198.75; TDEE x 1.55 = 3,408.1. Delta 1,430; raw 1,978.1. The 30% bound 2,385.6 sets it (the floor, 1,978.9, is below); rounded up to 2,390 so as not to cross it. Pace 1,018.1 x 7 / 7,700 = 0.93 kg a week, 0.71%. Protein 208 g; fat 0.40 x 1,558 / 9 = 69.2, 69 g; carbohydrate 233.7, 234 g.

The same rules reproduce the build plan's goldens: BMR 1,755.0 and 2,413.1; 2,150 kcal, P 126, F 73, C 247; 1,200 with clamps max_deficit and floor, 0.826%; 3,010; 2,410.

entrytitle.text: Entry points and components · Targets, recalculate, and the one new component

entrynotes.text:
Entry and component notes (S2, S6, S7).

setup: entry · targets-row. Targets as built (M3), with one new card above the fields: a ListRow "Estimate my targets" / "From a few questions about you and your goal", with the Calculator icon (to add to the icon map) and a chevron. It opens the wizard in recalculate mode, prefilled from the saved answers. Its name: "Estimate my targets, from a few questions about you and your goal". The rest of Targets is unchanged, including its note.

setup: entry · recalculate. Step 1 opened from Targets: the saved answer chosen (Male), no Back, Close on the right, no escape. Continue is live because every step is prefilled; the weight is the latest weigh-in's where there is one. Close on any step returns to Targets and keeps nothing. Existing accounts are never sent through the wizard (Zee, answer 2); this row is how they reach it.

setup: components. OptionCard, new: a radio card, at least 56 pt high, radius medium, surface fill with a 1 pt border, 12 pt by 16 pt padding, a 20 pt radio at the start. Chosen: accent border drawn 2 pt, accent-muted fill, filled radio. Optional: a description (caption, secondary, wraps), a Badge after the title, a trailing value with a muted caption. Disabled: radio and title at 40%, the reason at full strength with an Info icon, aria-disabled, the reason in its name. Role radio inside a radiogroup named by the question; press overlay and 0.96 scale; select haptic. Every option list in the wizard is OptionCards.

The step header is not a new component: SheetHeader's existing subtitle carries "Step n of 8" and the kit's ProgressBar sits under it. SheetHeader needs one extension: leading becomes optional (first run's step 1 has neither Back nor Close; the empty 44 pt slot keeps the title centred).
